sections.html:
Owners here usually weigh a regular listing against selling privately or accepting a cash bid. Listing works for a house in good shape when you can sit through showings and a buyer's loan process. Cash fits a house needing work, one with tenants, or a sale tied to a firm date, and it moves as fast as title and recording allow.

Most residents own. Owners occupy 75.6 percent of homes, with a median value of $635,600 for owner-occupied property. Population rose 8.2 percent between the April 2020 base and July 2025, to roughly 42,091 people.

Lake Stevens lies about 35 miles northeast of Seattle and 6 miles northeast of Everett, between Marysville and Snohomish. The city stands on a plateau over the Snohomish River delta, with the Cascade foothills to the east. Its namesake lake is the biggest and deepest in Snohomish County. Shopping centers on Frontier Village, at State Routes 9 and 204, and Cavalero Hill and Machias are among the named neighborhoods.

A household size near three suggests family buyers, and they usually check the school district, yard size and bedroom count first.

The Lake Stevens School District serves the city and part of southeastern Marysville. It has one high school, a mid-high school for grades 8 and 9, two middle schools and seven elementary schools.

Commutes run long, with a mean of 35.2 minutes. Three state highways cross the city: State Route 9, State Route 92 and State Route 204. Four roundabouts replaced the State Route 9 and 204 intersection in 2023. The Hewitt Avenue Trestle carries US 2 to Everett and is frequently congested. Community Transit provides bus service to Everett, Granite Falls, Lynnwood, Marysville and Snohomish, plus a peak-hour express to Lynnwood City Center station.

A 2018 estimate had 20 percent of working residents commuting to Everett, 13 percent to Seattle and 4 percent to Bellevue, with 6.3 percent working inside the city. Buyers who work in Everett or Seattle will price the drive, so a seller who can show a short route to the highway has something to talk about. Retail is concentrated at Frontier Village, and a Costco opened at State Route 9 and 20th Street Southeast in December 2022.

Stays shorter than 30 days fall under Lake Stevens Municipal Code 14.44.064 and Ordinance 1139. The limits the city lists are:

  • Residency: the owner or operator lives on site as a primary residence for at least 240 days a year, unless their permanent home is in the Lake Stevens Urban Growth Area.
  • Units: one rental per property, whether the main house, an accessory dwelling unit or a duplex unit.
  • Cap: 50 active licenses citywide, with permitted properties at least 150 feet apart.
  • Parking: one off-street stall for every two bedrooms, each at least nine feet by 19 feet.
  • Events: the rental cannot serve as a paid venue for weddings, banquets or fundraisers.

Both a city business license and a short-term rental permit are needed. The listed fees are $500 to apply and $100 a year to renew, and the city at (425) 622-9400 can confirm current amounts. If a buyer hopes to keep the rental income, the Planning and Community Development Department can say whether the permit travels with the property or must be reissued in the new owner's name.

sections.h2: If your house has a rental unit
sections.html:
Because the city allows the one permitted rental to be the main house, an accessory dwelling unit or a duplex unit, a property with a second unit raises a few extra questions at sale. Ask the Planning and Community Development Department what is on file for the address, including any business license and short-term rental permit. A buyer who plans to live in the main house and rent the other unit will want to know whether the permit can be transferred, and a buyer who wants no rental will want it closed out.

Keep leases, rent records and the permit paperwork together. Tenants have their own rights, so a cash buyer often asks for the lease terms before making an offer, and the closing date may depend on when the unit can be vacated or when the new owner takes over the lease.

sections.h2: How Snohomish County handles excise tax and recording
sections.html:
In Snohomish County, recording waits on the Treasurer's Office. Staff review each deed for real estate excise tax, and any tax owed must be paid in full first. That covers statutory warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, transfer on death deeds, personal representative deeds, trustee's deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure. The excise staff answer questions at 425-388-3366.

Sellers normally pay, and the due date is the sale date even if recording comes later. You will find the Recording Division in the Drewel Building, 3000 Rockefeller Avenue, Everett. Have escrow send the excise affidavit and the deed together to avoid a recording delay.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and contesting value
sections.html:
Payments open February 15. The county wants half by April 30 and half by October 31. Under RCW 84.56.020, skipping the first half makes the whole year delinquent, and interest or penalty then applies to the entire amount, posted on the first of each month. April 30, 2027 is the next first-half deadline.

An owner who disputes an assessed value must get a petition to the Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year, or inside the longer window printed on the notice. RCW 84.40.038 sets the filing rules and allows late filing in narrow cases. January 1 is the valuation date, so a sale at a price that differs sharply from the assessed value is a useful reference when you file.

sections.h2: What a Lake Stevens seller must disclose
sections.html: Among other items, the RCW 64.06.020 form asks about fire protection district coverage, roof leaks within five years and sewer service. Some Lake Stevens homes connect to the Lake Stevens Sewer District, so read your bill before you answer. Delivery starts a three business day window in which the buyer may rescind, unless both sides agreed otherwise in writing.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready to close
sections.html:
Washington does not require repairs, yet the disclosure form still asks about roof leaks and structural trouble. Buyers on a listing can negotiate fixes after the inspection, while a cash buyer can take the house as-is, which suits one that needs work.

Ahead of accepting any offer, request a payoff statement from every lender, look for open property tax halves and collect rental license or permit papers. Escrow adds up the payoff, excise tax, prorated property tax and other costs to reveal your net. Because the Treasurer's Office reviews the deed and affidavit before recording, ask escrow to submit both at once.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake Stevens house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers will take it as-is, and listing buyers can ask for repairs. Either way, the disclosure form covers roof leaks, structural problems and similar issues.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to keep a short-term rental in Lake Stevens?
faqs.a: Yes, a business license and a short-term rental permit, and only one rental unit per property. Check fees and transfer rules with the city before listing.

faqs.q: Who pays real estate excise tax on a Lake Stevens sale?
faqs.a: Usually the seller. The Snohomish County Treasurer's Office reviews the deed and collects the tax before it can be recorded.

faqs.q: When are Snohomish County property taxes due?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31, with payments accepted from February 15 on. Missing the first half makes the whole year delinquent.

faqs.q: How far is Lake Stevens from Everett and Seattle?
faqs.a: Roughly 6 miles northeast of Everett and 35 miles northeast of Seattle. The mean commute is 35.2 minutes.
